issue: Must a district court rehear disputed testimony before rejecting a magistrate judge's credibility findings on a suppression motion, or may it reject them on the written record?

sides.position: A district court must hold its own hearing and hear the disputed testimony before rejecting a magistrate judge's credibility determinations.
cases: McIntosh v. Wexford Health Sources, Inc., 987 F.3d 662 (7th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Scribner, 832 F.3d 252 (5th Cir. 2016)
United States v. Thoms, 684 F.3d 893 (9th Cir. 2012)
United States v. Powell, 628 F.3d 1254 (11th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Hernández-Rodríguez, 443 F.3d 138 (1st Cir. 2006)

sides.position: A district court need not rehear testimony unless the magistrate judge's credibility findings were dispositive or material to the district court's holding.
cases: United States v. Orrego-Fernandez, 78 F.3d 1497 (10th Cir. 1996)

quote: A circuit split exists as to whether a district court must rehear disputed testimony before rejecting a magistrate judge's credibility findings.
cite: United States v. Shue Moua, No. 24-2774 (8th Cir. 2025)
